briefing.headline: Midterms, mayoral bids and devolution debates dominate politics
briefing.overview: The US midterm elections saw massive spending and a shift in Senate control, while the UK Conservatives selected a London mayoral candidate and Wales and Scotland debated devolution‑related policies. Both sides of each issue present clear arguments.

stories.title: Conservatives pick London mayoral candidate
stories.what_happened: The Conservative Party chose former Home Secretary James Cleverly as its candidate for the 2028 London mayoral election, winning 86% support in a membership vote. The selection was announced on 19 November 2026.
stories.why_it_matters: The choice illustrates party leadership selection processes and the role of the executive in shaping local government, linking to the AQA topics of the Prime Minister, Cabinet and elections. It also shows how party structures influence candidate selection.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Party members say Cleverly’s experience will boost the Conservatives’ chances in a city that has voted Labour since 2016.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Opponents claim the selection favours establishment figures and ignores grassroots concerns about housing and transport.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: Right‑leaning commentators praise Cleverly’s law‑and‑order record as essential for London’s safety.

key_term.definition: The internal party process by which a person is chosen to stand for election.

stories.exam_use: Use as evidence of how party mechanisms affect executive influence in an essay on the relationship between parties and the executive.

stories.title: Scotland proposes mansion‑tax increase
stories.what_happened: Holyrood ministers published a bill to raise council tax on homes valued over £1 million, describing it as a ‘mansion tax’. The proposal moves forward in the Scottish Parliament.
stories.why_it_matters: The bill demonstrates devolution in action, showing how the Scottish Parliament can legislate on taxation, a key element of the AQA devolution topic. It also raises questions about fiscal autonomy versus UK‑wide policy.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Proponents say the tax will raise revenue for public services and address housing inequality.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Opponents warn it could discourage investment and hurt the property market.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Left‑leaning groups view it as a step toward progressive taxation.

key_term.definition: The transfer of powers from the central UK government to Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

stories.exam_use: Cite as evidence of devolved legislatures exercising fiscal powers in a comparative essay on UK devolution.

stories.title: Elon Musk regrets $442m midterm spend
stories.what_happened: Tesla CEO Elon Musk said he felt "pretty foolish" after spending $442 million on Republican campaigns in the 2026 midterm elections, which saw the GOP lose nine Senate seats. The spending did not prevent a Democratic majority.
stories.why_it_matters: The episode highlights the influence of private wealth on US elections and the limits of campaign spending, linking to the AQA US elections and parties topics. It also raises issues of political accountability.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Some say Musk’s spending reflects legitimate political participation by wealthy citizens.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Others argue it demonstrates how money can distort democratic outcomes.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Progressive voices view the spending as evidence for campaign finance reform.

key_term.definition: The fundraising and spending of money to influence election outcomes.

stories.exam_use: Use to illustrate arguments about the role of money in US elections in an essay on electoral fairness.

stories.title: Democrat Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate seat
stories.what_happened: Mary Peltola, a Democrat, defeated incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan to win Alaska’s Senate seat, giving Democrats a 56‑44 majority in the Senate. The result was the final Senate race of the 2026 midterms.
stories.why_it_matters: The win shifts the balance of power in Congress, illustrating how individual races affect party control, a core AQA US politics concept. It also shows regional political dynamics.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Democrats celebrate the victory as a sign of growing appeal in traditionally Republican states.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Republicans claim the result reflects national anti‑incumbent sentiment rather than a lasting shift.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: Conservative analysts warn the loss could lead to more progressive legislation.

key_term.definition: The party that holds more than half the seats in the US Senate, allowing it to control the agenda.

stories.exam_use: Reference in an essay on how party control of Congress influences policy making.

stories.title: Conservatives urge MPs to sign ECHR‑exit pledge
stories.what_happened: Conservative MPs were asked to sign a pledge supporting the UK’s departure from the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR). The move was reported on 18 November 2026.
stories.why_it_matters: The pledge touches on the relationship between domestic courts and international human‑rights law, linking to the AQA judiciary topic and debates over judicial sovereignty.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Proponents say leaving the ECHR would restore parliamentary sovereignty over human‑rights issues.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Opponents warn it could weaken protections for citizens and damage the UK’s international reputation.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Left‑wing groups view the pledge as an attack on civil liberties.

key_term.definition: The authority of a state to govern itself without external interference.

stories.exam_use: Use as evidence of tensions between domestic courts and international law in an essay on the UK judiciary.

stories.title: Trump team asks Supreme Court to block TPS ruling
stories.what_happened: The Trump administration filed a petition with the US Supreme Court seeking to overturn a lower‑court decision that kept Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Venezuelan nationals in place. The request was made on 18 November 2026.
stories.why_it_matters: The case illustrates the Supreme Court’s role in reviewing executive actions and immigration policy, relevant to the AQA US courts and executive topics. It also raises questions about checks and balances.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Administration officials claim the lower court overstepped its authority.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Immigration advocates say the move threatens vulnerable migrants.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: Conservative commentators view the petition as defending executive prerogative.

key_term.definition: The process by which courts examine the legality of actions by the executive or legislature.

stories.exam_use: Cite in an essay on the separation of powers and the courts’ check on the executive.

compare.uk: The Conservative Party’s selection of James Cleverly as London mayoral candidate shows internal party mechanisms shaping local elections.
compare.us: The 2026 US midterms resulted in a Democratic Senate majority after extensive private spending, highlighting the impact of campaign finance on national elections.
compare.insight: The contrast reveals that UK elections are heavily influenced by party structures, whereas US elections are more affected by individual donor spending and broader national swings.

ideas_lens.text: The Conservative push to leave the ECHR reflects a core conservative belief in national sovereignty and limited external constraints, echoing Edmund Burke’s emphasis on tradition and cautious reform.

exam_question.question: Assess the extent to which party structures influence electoral outcomes in the UK and the US.
exam_question.tip: Compare the Conservative mayoral selection process with US campaign‑finance dynamics, using the Cleverly and Musk stories as evidence.
